commitResults.messageBody:
The starter application still uses Duke as its chatbot name, which
does not reflect the chosen project identity.

Rename the chatbot to CLANKER and update the related project
documentation.

Using one name across the application and documentation avoids
confusing users about the identity of the project.

The chatbot starts without a friendly introduction, so users receive
no context about what the program does.

Add a greeting and farewell message to make the interaction clearer
and more welcoming.

Keeping these messages with the chatbot startup flow gives users
immediate feedback when the application starts and ends.

commitResults.messageTitle: CLANKER: Add startup banner and personality
commitResults.messageBody:
The command-line interface lacks a recognizable visual identity when
it starts.

Add a CLANKER banner and display it during startup to make the
application easier to identify.

A consistent startup presentation makes the chatbot feel like a
coherent application as more commands are added.

commitResults.messageTitle: Commands: Echo input and support bye
commitResults.messageBody:
The chatbot does not yet respond to user input or provide a way to
end the session.

Echo each entered command and terminate the interaction when the user
enters bye.

These behaviours establish the basic command-loop interaction needed
for subsequent features.

The chatbot can receive input but does not retain tasks or show them
back to the user.

Support adding tasks to an in-memory list and listing them with their
positions.

Keeping task storage and display together provides the foundation for
later task-management commands.

Tasks have no shared representation or way to record whether they are
complete.

Introduce a Task class and add mark and unmark commands for updating
task status.

A shared task abstraction keeps completion behaviour consistent as
more task types are added.

commitResults.messageTitle: Code quality: Follow Java naming conventions
commitResults.messageBody:
Several identifiers do not follow the Java naming conventions used by
the project.

Rename the affected identifiers to follow the established Java style.

Consistent naming makes the code easier to scan and reduces the effort
needed to understand unfamiliar parts of the program.

commitResults.messageTitle: Task types: Add todos, deadlines, and events
commitResults.messageBody:
The task manager supports only one generic task type, so users cannot
record deadlines or events.

Add todo, deadline, and event task types with the corresponding input
commands.

Specialized task types let users capture different kinds of work while
keeping them together in one task list.

commitResults.messageTitle: Refactor command processing out of main
commitResults.messageBody:
The main method handles application setup, input-loop control, command
parsing, and task updates, making the program harder to read and
maintain.

Extract command processing into a dedicated helper method.

Separating these responsibilities makes the input loop easier to
understand while preserving the existing command behaviour.
